blocks.content: Assuming the frequency of S is at its selective equilibrium, what is the strength of selection against NN individuals due to malaria? Writing the fitnesses of the SS, SN, and NN genotypes as 1 - t, 1, and 1 - s respectively, the result from Example 5.4 is an equilibrium frequency of $ s/(s + t) $ for allele S. Setting this equal to 0.123 implies that $$ t=\frac{(1-0.123)}{0.123}s=7.120s\quad or\quad s=0.140t $$

If SS individuals are either lethal (t = 1) or have only 10% fitness (t = 0.9), then s = 0.140 and 0.126, respectively. In other words, relative to NN individuals, heterozygotes have a 13% to 14% fitness advantage due to increased malaria resistance.
